newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS / Quiet October expiration.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS / Quiet October expiration.

text.p: U.S. stock index options saw high volume but little price movement ahead of the October contract expirations, traders said.
Most October index and individual equity options expire on Saturday after last trading today, while Chicago Mercantile Exchange's S&P 500 futures options expire today.

"A rather surprisingly dull October expiration it's turning out to be right now," said Jesse Stamer, a general partner of TradeNet and designated primary market-maker at the Chicago Board Options Exchange.
"It doesn't look like there's a lot of open interest in OEX (S&P 100 index .OEX ), which has a tendency to cut down on the size of the roll whichever way it might be," he added.
CBOE volatility index .VIX hovered in familiar territory at 16.61 at 1200 CDT/1700 GMT, up 0.10 point. OEX was up 1.12 points at 686.68.
Traders added that early exercise for October contracts had been benign throughout this expiration week.
According to CBOE, early exercise in October OEX calls on Thursday totaled 451 contracts, while that in puts amounted to 750 contracts. There was no early exercise on Wednesday.
Stamer said he expected volatility to pick up next week once the market gets over the expiration.
"It appears to me that November volatility is picking up over the value ot October and that we will have some action over the next couple of weeks," he said.
But some traders expected volatilities to stay subdued as long as the market's underlying bullish sentiment persisted.
"The biggest loss it (OEX) has had in the last five trading sessions is 40 cents (0.40 point)," said Jerry Hegarty, chief equity analyst at Thomson Research.
"So there isn't a lot of volatility...because the downside is just not getting much play," he said. "Each day seems to be a question of how much they're going to rally."
Still, a brokerage trader at CBOE said the weakness in the technology sector since mid-week could eventually spill over to the broader market.

Technology shares were mostly softer today due in part to consolidation after recent rallies, traders said. News that Soundview downgraded its short-term rating of Microsoft Corp to hold from buy also weighed on the sector.
Microsoft shares were off 1-1/8 to 134-3/8 in early afternoon trade.
CBOE technology index .TXX was down 0.31 point at 184.42, while Philadelphia Stock Exchange semiconductor index .SOXX lost 1.59 to 195.60.
Hegarty noted the overall market has made handsome gains this year all in all, despite the slump in the technology sector, which is still well off its peaks in late 1995.
"I don't put a lot of weight on that," he said.
